prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1083; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Received first notice of loss by phone from the insured driver. Insured reports a sideswipe while changing lanes on a multi-lane roadway. Other vehicle departed the scene before exchange of information. Insured reports a passenger-side scrape and states the other driver may have been in the adjacent lane. Opened file and requested the insured's statement, photos of damage, and any dashcam footage.

Entry 2: Obtained recorded statement from insured. Insured confirms signaling before moving over and noticing a vehicle close to the rear quarter panel. Witness contact information noted on the police report, but witness has not yet responded to outreach. Requested the police report and nearby traffic camera footage through the appropriate channels.

Entry 3: Claimant has retained counsel, who has notified this office that the claimant sustained a wrist fracture and is seeking medical payments coverage and a bodily injury evaluation. Requested authorization for medical records and itemized bills. Counsel asked that all future contact be directed to their office. Reserves adjusted to reflect a possible bodily injury exposure pending records review.

Entry 4: Reviewed the police report. Responding officer documented the sideswipe location and noted the other vehicle as unidentified. Officer's narrative supports the insured's account that the collision occurred during a lane change. Liability assessment currently leans toward the other driver, pending confirmation of the unidentified vehicle's involvement. Follow-up request sent to the reporting agency for supplemental information.

Entry 5: Received medical records from claimant's counsel. Records confirm a distal radius fracture treated with immobilization and a follow-up orthopedic consult is scheduled. Treating physician's notes indicate expected recovery timeline is still being assessed. Referred the file to the bodily injury unit for evaluation. Scheduled a file review in 30 days to confirm receipt of remaining bills and any further treatment updates.
